🚨🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM GOVT OFFERS CNTE THE HEAD OF USICAMM</u>

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez and Education Secretary Mario Delgado handed CNTE a concrete roadmap to dismantle USICAMM — the punitive teacher-evaluation institution born from Peña Nieto's 2013 educational reform — and to overhaul the 2007 ISSSTE pension law that gutted teacher retirements.

Timeline per Contralínea: June 15 working table; June 16-20 diagnostic phase; Aug 18-31 democratic teacher consultation; September 14 sent to Congress. "El gobierno federal mantiene abiertas las puertas del diálogo," Rodríguez said. Delgado: "Ya pasaron 19 meses y cada que nos reunimos: 'maestros hay que hacer la mesa.'" The neoliberal teaching architecture CNTE has fought for a decade — finally on the table.

Source: Contralínea

🔥🇲🇽 <u>CALDERÓN STILL GOVERNS CHIHUAHUA — VIA MARU CAMPOS</u>

La Jornada confirms: Felipe Calderón Hinojosa governs Chihuahua de facto through PAN Governor María Eugenia Campos Galván. Her state finances are run by Calderón's ex-finance secretary Ernesto Cordero Arroyo. Her legal advisor — even on personal business matters — is Roberto Gil Zuarth, Calderón's former legislative coordinator.

Campos Galván "works only Wednesdays every other week, after noon" and skips state security meetings, the paper reports. Same governor who days ago hosted Vicente Fox and Calderón to denounce Morena for "handing power to the cartels." The narco-PAN dynasty refuses to die.

Source: La Jornada

🔥🇲🇽 <u>BANKS POCKET RECORD 104 BILLION PESOS — Q1 2026 PROFITS BLOW PAST EVERY PRIOR YEAR</u>

Private banks operating in Mexico raked in 104.74 billion pesos in profits between January and April 2026 — the largest figure for that period since records exist, according to the CNBV. The eight systemically important banks — BBVA Mexico, Banorte, Santander, Banamex, Inbursa, Scotiabank, HSBC and Citi Mexico — alone took 87.87 billion, a 29.55% nominal jump from 67.83 billion in the same period of 2025.

The total credit portfolio of private banking reached 8.28 trillion pesos, just 1.94% higher in real terms. Profits explode; lending barely moves. Foreign banks. Mexican spreads. Working class pays.

Source: La Jornada

AUTOMOTIVE NEWS: VW Group of America Seeks Lower Mexico Tariffs as It Revamps U.S. Lineup
June 4, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Automotive News: VW Group of America CEO Kjell Gruner is now lobbying for LOWER tariffs on Mexico-built vehicles after Trump's 25% import duty hit the Jetta and Taos. Same auto industry that lobbied for tariffs to "protect American jobs" now wants them gone — because their US Chattanooga expansion can't survive without Mexico's supply chain. 💀

The contradiction is on the record: tariffs don't bring jobs back, they raise prices for US consumers and break US factories. VW held US pricing through June; it can't anymore. 🇲🇽

• 25% duty on Mexico-built Jetta and Taos
• Chattanooga plant expansion depends on Mexico-sourced components
• VW pricing guarantee expires in June; consumer prices rising next

LATIN TIMES / CNBC: The World Cup Shadow — Mexico Teachers' Union Strike Escalates
June 3, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Latin Times and CNBC frame the CNTE teachers' strike as a World Cup spoiler — "if there's no solution, the ball won't roll" — burying the actual demands: repeal of the 2007 ISSSTE pension reform, 100% wage adjustment, reversal of neoliberal education reforms. 🔍

CNTE has struck under every Mexican president for two decades. The June 11 opening-match timing is leverage. US framing treats teachers as hostage-takers — not workers using the most-watched event on Earth to make 20-year-old grievances visible. 🇲🇽

• "Escalates dramatically," "crossed into new territory" — escalation language for a labor dispute
• Sheinbaum: "What do they want? Repression. There will be no repression."
• Five rounds of working-group talks held with Interior, SEP and ISSSTE before strike escalated

BLOOMBERG / LATIN TIMES: Sheinbaum Unveils Affordable EV Prototype Backed by Government
June 7, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Bloomberg calls Mexico's Olinia 1 — 150,000 pesos (~$7,500), 125 km range, six-seat, designed by IPN and TecNM researchers — a "government-backed prototype" rather than what it is: Mexico's first homegrown electric car, built around domestic supply chains as Trump tariffs gut auto trade. 🇲🇽

Production starts in Puebla in 2027. 50% domestic components today, target 75% by 2030. Sheinbaum: "When Mexico trusts in the intelligence and creativity of its people, there is no limit." Olinia = Nahuatl for "to move." 🔍

• Bloomberg headline: "prototype backed by government" — not "first national EV"
• Most US outlets ignored the launch entirely; Latin Times and Benzinga did briefs
• Same week US press flooded coverage with cartel/World Cup fear stories

JACOBIN: The CIA Is Up to No Good in Mexico
June 6, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Kurt Hackbarth in Jacobin on the CIA agents killed April 19 in Chihuahua: Trump's strategy is "stamp out every remaining progressive government in Latin America" and replace them with "far-right lackeys, stooges, criminals, and sellouts." 🇲🇽

CIA operating inside Mexico violates Mexican law. AP confirmed the agents' identities weeks ago — most US mainstream press has buried the story since. Sheinbaum has requested zero extraditions from the US despite Mexico submitting 269 to Washington since 2018. 💀

• "serve as an advance force for an eventual US invasion?"
• "Track down strategic mineral sites? Organize destabilization cells?"
• Sheinbaum demanded "evidence based in Mexican law"

🚨🇲🇽 <u>TRUMP'S TARIFFS DESTROYED 213,000 NORTH AMERICAN MANUFACTURING JOBS IN ONE YEAR — ECONOMÍA</u>

Mexico's Secretaría de Economía data, via El Economista: 111,347 Mexican manufacturing jobs and 102,000 US manufacturing jobs vanished between Feb 2025 and Feb 2026 — combined ~213,000 industrial positions destroyed by the tariff war. Heaviest losses: transport equipment, wood, plastics, rubber, and machinery. Economía's framing: "in many industries Mexico, the US, and Canada produce as a single integrated economy," so taxing every border crossing kills jobs in all three countries at once. Sheinbaum had already attributed 227,155 Mexican Q1 job losses to Trump's measures.

The "America First" tariff doctrine destroyed more US factory jobs than it created. The data is the indictment.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>FOVISSSTE GETS ITS CONSTRUCTOR POWERS BACK — 100,000 PUBLIC HOUSING UNITS COMING</u>

DOF published Friday June 5 the new Organic Regulation that returns FOVISSSTE — the state workers' housing fund — its historic faculty to build, rent, and sell housing directly. The neoliberal Infonavit/FOVISSSTE model since the 90s was credit-only: hand workers loans, let private developers warehouse the supply at whatever price. The new structure targets 100,000 units under the Vivienda para el Bienestar program, with fresh Subdirections of Vivienda, Financing Schemes, and Beneficiary Rights to run construction directly.

Forty years of "the market provides" replaced with the state building homes again.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>LATINUS-LINKED FIRM CHARGED IMSS BIENESTAR 200% OVER MARKET FOR DIALYSIS — THEN PULLED PLUG ON PATIENTS</u>

Zdenko SA de CV — under UIF investigation since 2023 for influence trafficking and money laundering, with reported payments to LatinUs and BCG Limited Consulting — was billing IMSS Bienestar 2,200 pesos per hemodialysis session when the market rate is 800. That's 200 percent over competitors and ~100 million pesos in Puebla alone for 2025. When IMSS ran the comparison and cancelled appointments, Zdenko unilaterally suspended treatment in June and November 2025. Related vendor BITA pulled the same move on 971 patients in State of Mexico.

The same right-wing media circuit that screams about "4T corruption" was getting paid 200 percent above market to keep kidney patients alive.
